period_searched: November 11-13, 2026 (several reports cover incidents and campaigns from August-October 2026)

incidents.victim: Telecommunications carriers (Taiwan and five other countries)
incidents.vector: Exploited SS7 and Diameter signaling-protocol backdoors planted inside hacked telecom infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Enabled covert tracking of subscriber locations and interception of calls and SMS for a small number of high-value targets, including political figures, across telcos in six countries, mostly in Taiwan.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency/Web3 professionals and open-source software maintainers
incidents.vector: Deepfake video-call social engineering ("FaceStealer") lured targets into fake meetings where a staged technical error prompted installation of malware.
incidents.impact: Stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months and compromised open-source maintainers to enable software supply-chain attacks; DOJ seized the scheme's cloud infrastructure and over 900 webcam videos used to impersonate victims.

incidents.vector: Abused a flawed third-party ScreenConnect extension (RMM+) whose authentication key defaulted to blank, letting an attacker bypass MFA and push rogue remote-access clients.
incidents.impact: Installed malicious ScreenConnect clients on 288 endpoints within 90 minutes, positioning attacker-controlled remote access that mimicked legitimate software; ConnectWise disabled the extension across roughly 400 partner environments.

incidents.vector: Ransomware encryption of cloud infrastructure, following similar recent attacks on Russian hosting providers ESTT and Beget.
incidents.impact: Disrupted cloud hosting, corporate email and virtual servers for business customers across Belarus for several days; no evidence of customer data theft found.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack claimed by the BYOD ransomware gang, which also recently hit Michigan State University and the University of New Mexico.
incidents.impact: Forced university-wide device shutdowns and WiFi disconnection; full restoration of normal operations expected to take multiple weeks.

incidents.victim: City of Osaka residents and roughly 400 Japanese organizations using Arara's email service
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Arara's email distribution service, used by TKC Corporation's administrative platform and other customers including Sega.
incidents.impact: Exposed over 1 million Osaka resident email addresses and 77 million addresses across nearly 400 Japanese organizations; the stolen service was used to send millions of phishing emails impersonating financial institutions.

incidents.vector: Compromised three developers (a trojanized Homebrew download and a fake job-interview assignment) to obtain signing privileges, then exploited Ethereum EIP-7702 smart-account authorizations to install a malicious "sweeper" that redirected wallet funds.
incidents.impact: Stole roughly $6.34 billion across 11 wallets; standing on-chain authorizations let the theft continue for about four hours after detection. DOJ and partners have since frozen over $2.7 billion and obtained court authorization to seize $1.2 billion.

incidents.vector: Ransomware/data-theft attack claimed by the Qilin ransomware-as-a-service gang.
incidents.impact: Personal information of students and employees was stolen; the university took its MachForms portal offline and is still identifying affected individuals.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries (Latin America, Europe, Asia, Middle East), a Middle East interior ministry, and semiconductor, defense and telecom organizations
incidents.vector: Used the open-source, autonomous multi-agent ARTEX pentesting/C2 framework to run parallel, high-speed intrusion attempts against web apps, cloud services, VPNs and mail infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Targeted over 200 organizations in 11 days; confirmed post-exploitation access at nine organizations, including two extensive intrusions into Latin American foreign ministries and compromise of a Middle East interior ministry.

incidents.victim: French retail chains (Intermarché, Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour) and food producers
incidents.vector: Compromised internet-exposed Danfoss refrigeration control panels to remotely set freezer temperatures to extreme highs.
incidents.impact: Hit 700 stores plus food factories and a slaughterhouse; spoiled food and triggered fires at 15 locations, causing tens of millions of euros in losses. French officials attributed the attack to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit, though US intelligence holds only low confidence in that attribution.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor supply-chain companies, defense-policy organizations, and civil-society groups (19 targeted, 10 compromised)
incidents.vector: Operators supplied a target and goal to the open-source Cairn autonomous AI pentesting framework (paired with Chinese models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek), which independently planned, executed and recorded attacks.
incidents.impact: Gained unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 of 19 targeted organizations, including mass exposure of over one million records at a US teachers' union, creation of persistent admin accounts at a semiconductor company, and tampering with a live industry-standards ballot document.

incidents.victim: Government ministries and law-enforcement agencies in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries
incidents.vector: Injected malicious JavaScript into webmail portals and government web applications to sideload malicious browser extensions via the "Falcon" (XG) command-and-control framework.
incidents.impact: Stole passwords, emails, session cookies and communications from compromised government users across ministries of foreign affairs, defense and interior, and law enforcement agencies; also delivered a OneDrive-based secondary implant (Antino).
